discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 202642e: parseStatus now keeps the original path on R/C records (originalPath on the file entry). The webview includes it in unstage actions (unstagePaths helper, used for row, group, and breadcrumb unstage) and passes it to get_git_file_diff so a staged rename reads HEAD at the old path. Covered by a real-repo test that git mv's a file, checks the diff shows the old contents, unstages both paths, and verifies the old path is no longer staged as a deletion.
Fixed in 202642e: numstat records split on the first two tabs only and the remainder is kept as the filename, with a test for a tab-containing name.

Valid, and fixed in 1690c40bf. I removed the cap. Each failure record is what stops its run from falling back to an earlier checkpoint, so failures now persist for the life of the session, as checkpoint history does. Covered by `keeps every failure so no failed run falls back to an earlier checkpoint` in `checkpoint-records.test.ts`; it fails if the cap is put back.

Valid, fixed. A link whose target is a directory already on the current copy chain, or an ancestor of one (`.`, `..`, a sibling that links back), is now skipped and listed in `skippedPaths` instead of being expanded again, and the number of linked-directory expansions is capped (`MAX_LINK_EXPANSIONS`). Covered by "skips links that loop back into a directory being copied": twenty links to `.` plus one to `..` finish in well under a second with only the real content copied.

Fixed. An entry whose value is an inline scalar, like `disabled: true` or `disabled: false # note`, is now a single line, so an indented comment after it stays with the author. Block scalars (`|`, `>`) and nested values still take their indented continuation lines with them. Test added for both disabling and re-enabling.

Fixed in 2c1a7f7d7: normalization now recurses into `items` (object and tuple forms) and into `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf` branches before the object-likeness gate, so nested uppercase types lowercase at every depth. Covered by the new "normalizes nested array items and combinator branches" test.

Intentional tradeoff. A cut-off stream whose last 2k non-whitespace chars are pure 0/1 is rare, and it fails with a clear error rather than stopping silently. Loosening the check to allow it would weaken detection of the real repetition-loop case, so leaving it as is.
